name: Sherman–Morrison rank-one linear-system update
definition: Given invertible A and A+uvᵀ, solve Ay=b and Az=u; x=y−z(vᵀy)/(1+vᵀz).
variables: A base matrix; u,v update vectors; b right side; y,z base solves
assumptions: Real nonsingular square A; conforming vectors; d=1+vᵀz nonzero; accurate base solves and finite arithmetic.
limitations: Cancellation or small update denominator can amplify numerical error; reuse of a factorization is needed for the usual cost advantage.
failure_conditions: Zero or near-zero denominator; failed residual check
computation: Solve using existing factors without explicitly forming an inverse; reject a numerically unsafe denominator and check the updated-system residual.

source.citation: Nicholas J. Higham (2020), What Is the Sherman–Morrison–Woodbury Formula?, rank-one identity and factorization discussion. https://nhigham.com/2020/09/29/what-is-the-sherman-morrison-woodbury-formula/

required_inputs: Base matrix or factorization, right side and update vectors.
incompatible_methods: Ignoring singularity of the updated matrix
mechanism_note: The rank-one correction reuses base solves instead of factoring the modified matrix. In exact arithmetic, substituting the formula yields (A+uvᵀ)x=b whenever the denominator is nonzero.

name: Block orthogonal eigeniteration
definition: For n by p orthonormal Q₀ and 1<p<n, compute Z=AQ_k and thin QR Z=Q_(k+1)R_(k+1). Set H_k=Q_kᵀAQ_k and monitor ||AQ_k−Q_kH_k||; return a basis for the target invariant subspace only after convergence checks.
variables: A matrix; p block dimension; Q orthonormal basis; R triangular factor
assumptions: Real symmetric A; strict gap |λ_p|>|λ_(p+1)| in descending magnitude; nonsingular projection of Q₀ onto the leading p eigenvectors; rank-preserving QR and finite iteration limit.
limitations: A small invariant-subspace residual alone cannot certify that the subspace is dominant; a narrow spectral gap slows convergence.
failure_conditions: Rank loss or invariant-subspace residual failure
computation: Alternate block multiplication and QR; check invariant-subspace residual.

source.citation: David Bindel (2025), Cornell CS 6210 Matrix Computations, Power method and subspace iteration, 27 October, section Subspaces and orthogonal iteration. https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs6210/2025fa/lec/2025-10-27.html

required_inputs: Matrix, starting orthonormal block, tolerance and iteration limit.
incompatible_methods: Claiming individual eigenvector convergence without appropriate gaps
mechanism_note: Block generalization of power iteration: spans are those of A^kQ₀ in exact arithmetic. p=1 is power iteration; full square orthogonal iteration is related to unshifted QR. Restrict to 1<p<n and count only as a variant.
